elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Garman further warrants that the Maintenance Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner..." — express workmanlike standard for the services.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 12: "Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects." The warranted item is expressly the Software and the benchmark is the Specifications (its documentation).

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: "For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services..." — one year equals 12 months, plus a continuing tail.
The inserted services warranty runs "for a period of thirty (30) calendar days following their performance"; 30 days is the fallback duration, not the preferred 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Sparkling's remedy ... is, at Garman's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Software or Maintenance Services..."
Inserted: "...or a refund of the fees paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears anywhere in the rendered Section 12 or the inserted sentences.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty appears in the rendered operative language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 12 warrants Software conformance with the Specifications for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date — well beyond 90 days, and expressly a software-to-specifications warranty.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted: Maintenance Services "shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner for a period of thirty (30) calendar days following their performance."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence expressly offers "repair or replacement of the non-conforming Software or Maintenance Services" for breach of the Section 12 warranties.
Inserted remedy sentence expressly offers "a refund of the fees paid for them."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the retained one-year Software-to-Specifications warranty covers the ≥90-day software element, and the two inserted sentences supply the 30-day services warranty and the repair/replacement/refund remedy that the Agreement previously lacked (Section 10(c) repair was a maintenance obligation, not a warranty remedy).

Preferred level is not reached: the services warranty is 30 days rather than 90, and there is no compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty and no no-malicious-code warranty. To move to preferred the drafter would need to change "thirty (30) calendar days" to "ninety (90) days" and add express law-compliance and malicious-code warranties.

Minimality holds: two inserted sentences tracking the playbook model language, no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural extras, and the favourable existing one-year (and continuing) Software warranty and the Section 10(c) no-charge repair obligation are left intact. The "professional and workmanlike" standard in the services sentence is the necessary substantive content of a services warranty, not an extra.

Intent is preserved: no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is disturbed; the fee-charging carve-out in Section 10(c) and the Fee Schedule reference survive unchanged. One drafting caution (not a failure): Section 12 covers "the acceptance period", and the retained acceptance/rejection remedy in Sections 7–8 is stated to be "in lieu of any other remedy", so consider opening the inserted remedy sentence with "Except as provided in Sections 7 and 8," to avoid any argument of overlap during acceptance.
Note that the remedy election sits "at Garman's option", which matches the playbook model language but is the vendor-favourable variant; it does not defeat the remedy elements.
